discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics (moire materials, flat-band superconductivity)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. The discovery created the field of twistronics: a tunable platform in which density, twist and fields control strongly correlated and topological phases, including orbital magnetism, fractional Chern insulators and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect, now reproduced in many moire systems. It also revealed that superconductivity in flat bands is governed by the quantum geometry of Bloch states, linking band topology to superfluidity. A striking theoretical prediction confirmed across numerous platforms, it opened an entirely new direction in quantum materials.
